chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Fadalah from Ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked him about the call to prayer (Adhan) before the rising of dawn (Fajr). He said, 'There is no harm with it. As for the Sunnah, it is with the dawn, and indeed that benefits the neighbors,' meaning before the dawn.
Al-Shaykh (may God have mercy on him) said: And there is no harm for a person to give the Adhan while he is without ablution (wudu), but he does not give the Iqamah except while he is upon ablution.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to give the Adhan before Fajr without performing ablution?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between the pre-dawn Adhan, which is permissible and socially beneficial for neighbors, and the Sunnah Adhan coinciding with true dawn. Shaykh al-Tusi adds a nuanced juristic detail: while ritual purity (wudu) is not required for the Adhan itself, it is mandatory for the Iqamah, reflecting the transition from announcement to the immediate commencement of prayer. This highlights the practical flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding the conditions of the caller to prayer.
